Splitting up the integral into the difference of two integrals and evaluating each integral separately, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}(y-\frac{1}{{y}^{2}})\text{d}y & ={\int }_{1}^{2}y\,\text{d}y-{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}\,{|}_{1}^{2}+\frac{1}{y}\,{|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({2}^{2}-{1}^{2})+(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{1}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(3)+(\frac{1}{2}-1) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}-\frac{1}{2} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
